facts.fact_text: On 3 February 2009 the first and the second applicants organised a protest demonstration in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
From the video submitted by the parties, it appears that approximately twenty individuals took part in the demonstration on 3 February 2009 in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
The third applicant was among the participants in the demonstration on 3 February 2009 in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
Several minutes after the beginning of the demonstration on 3 February 2009, the protesters were attacked by six men wearing masks.
From the very beginning of the gathering on 3 February 2009, four uniformed police officers observed the event from a patrol car parked close to the place of the event.
According to the applicants, the approximately six people in plain clothes who filmed the event on 3 February 2009 were police officers.
The Government denied that the approximately six people in plain clothes who filmed the event on 3 February 2009 were police officers.
When the clash between the protesters and the attackers began on 3 February 2009, no police officer intervened.
The protesters called the police and requested assistance during the attack on 3 February 2009, but received no assistance.
A police patrol appeared only one hour and a half after the attack began on 3 February 2009.
The police patrol that arrived one hour and a half after the attack began on 3 February 2009 took the two immobilised attackers into custody.

On 2 February 2009 the first and the second applicants lodged a notification with the municipal authorities stating their intention to conduct a demonstration in front of the Prosecutor General's Office, followed by a march to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and a demonstration in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
In the notification lodged on 2 February 2009, the first and the second applicants described the planned event as a spontaneous reaction to the events of 29 January 2009.
In the notification lodged on 2 February 2009, the first and the second applicants relied on Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 2008.
According to Section 10 of the Assemblies Act of 2008, the organisers of a demonstration must notify the local authorities five days in advance about the planned demonstration.
Under Article 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 2008, no obligation to notify local authorities five days in advance exists for spontaneous demonstrations.
Under Article 12(5) of the Assemblies Act of 2008, no obligation to notify local authorities five days in advance exists for demonstrations with fewer than fifty participants.

According to Article 67 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the failure by organisers of a demonstration to notify the local authorities in accordance with the provisions of the Assemblies Act of 2008 is punishable with a fine of up to 800 Moldovan Lei.
The fine of up to 800 Moldovan Lei under Article 67 of the Code of Administrative Offences was the equivalent of approximately 50 euros at the time of the events.
When the clash between the protesters and the attackers began on 3 February 2009, no police officer intervened.
The protesters called the police and requested assistance during the attack on 3 February 2009, but received no assistance.
A police patrol appeared only one hour and a half after the attack began on 3 February 2009.
No action was taken in respect of the applicants' complaint about the inaction of the police during the attack on 3 February 2009.
